description: Permissions the yt2mp window needs: a native save dialog, a file picker so the converter tab can take files already on disk, revealing a finished file in the file manager, opening a post's original page in the user's browser (the only way to view TikTok/Instagram/X/Twitch content, which can't be embedded), and installing a signed update then restarting into it. github.com is allowed so a release page can be opened — on Linux an AppImage that wasn't launched as an AppImage cannot self-update, so it links to the download instead. Everything else (yt-dlp, the filesystem, the network) is reached through this app's own commands, never exposed to the webview directly. It is granted to the app's own webview by label, not to the main window: the built-in browser's tabs are child webviews of that window, and naming the window would hand every site open in a tab the same permissions. Every app command is listed because each one needs a permission (see build.rs); the tabs get none of them.
